aliases.name: Abraham's Ax
aliases.vendor: Secureworks (persona linked to the same operator)

identification.summary: Marigold Sandstorm is Microsoft's name for an Iran-origin actor that Microsoft previously tracked as DEV-500 (DEV-0500) [S4][S5]. MITRE ATT&CK maps Marigold Sandstorm and DEV-0500 to Moses Staff (G1009), a suspected Iranian group that has mainly targeted Israeli companies since at least September 2021 and says it aims to cause damage by leaking stolen data and encrypting networks without demanding a ransom [S1][S2]. Microsoft's February 2024 Iran report calls Moses Staff an 'IRGC-run cyber persona' [S8]. Secureworks tracks the operator behind the Moses Staff and Abraham's Ax personas as COBALT SAPLING [S10].
identification.firstObserved: MITRE: active since at least September 2021 [S1]. Kaspersky says Moses Staff was first seen on underground forums in September 2021 [S11].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Marigold Sandstorm (formerly DEV-500). Microsoft's mapping file lists DEV-500 and VENGEFUL KITTEN as other names but not 'Moses Staff' [S4]. The Sandstorm family name denotes Iran attribution [S5]. The Moses Staff equivalence comes from MITRE ATT&CK, which cites Microsoft's July 2023 naming page [S1][S6], and from MISP Galaxy [S7]. Microsoft's February 2024 report refers to 'Moses Staff' as a persona and does not use the name Marigold Sandstorm [S8]. Abraham's Ax (from November 2022) is a second persona that Secureworks assesses is likely run by the same operator (COBALT SAPLING) [S10].

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft describes Moses Staff as an IRGC-run cyber persona [S8], and its naming taxonomy places Marigold Sandstorm in the Iran (Sandstorm) family [S4][S5]. Secureworks believes COBALT SAPLING is Iranian in origin [S10]. MITRE uses 'suspected Iranian' [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft states the IRGC link as fact in a February 2024 report but does not give a confidence level in the passage reviewed [S8]. Secureworks assesses the Moses Staff/Abraham's Ax link as likely [S10]. MITRE ATT&CK hedges ('suspected Iranian') [S1]. Kaspersky refers to Moses Staff as 'alleged to be an Iranian hacker group' [S11]. The sources gathered contain no US or Israeli government attribution.
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Intelligence assessment [S8] and naming mapping [S4]. Secureworks CTU analysis of shared iconography, videography, leak sites and malware artifacts [S10]. Technical reporting by Check Point (November 2021) and Cybereason (February 2022), as summarized by MITRE [S1][S2][S3].

objectives: Politically motivated disruption and hack-and-leak operations. Moses Staff openly states it aims to damage Israeli companies by leaking stolen data and encrypting networks without asking for a ransom [S1][S2]. Microsoft places the persona inside Iran's IRGC-run cyber-enabled influence activity [S8]. Secureworks reports that the Abraham's Ax persona targets Saudi government ministries. It assesses this is likely a response to Saudi Arabia's leadership role in improving relations between Israel and Arab states. Secureworks adds that such personas give the Government of Iran plausible deniability [S10].

regions: Italy, India, Germany, Chile, Turkey, the UAE and the United States [S1][S3]
targeting.notes: Israeli companies are the primary focus [S1][S2]. Targeting outside Israel and the sector list come from Cybereason's February 2022 reporting, as summarized by MITRE [S1][S3]. Saudi targeting is attributed to the Abraham's Ax persona, which Secureworks links to the same operator [S10]. Several victim claims (an Israeli power plant, a defense ministry, security cameras) are the persona's own claims and are only partly confirmed [S8][S12][S13].

capabilities.summary: Initial access through known vulnerabilities in internet-facing infrastructure such as Microsoft Exchange, followed by obfuscated ASPX web shells [S1][S2]. PyDCrypt is a PyInstaller-compiled loader tailored to each victim. It opens firewall rules for SMB, NetBIOS and RPC to spread through the network, then drops DCSrv [S1][S2]. DCSrv is a time-triggered encryptor built on the open-source DiskCryptor and its signed drivers. It encrypts whole drives and offers no ransom path, so it works as a wiper [S1][S2]. PsExec is used for lateral movement [S1]. Since at least November 2021 the group has used StrifeWater, a reconnaissance RAT with screenshot, file-collection and module-download functions [S1][S3]. Stolen data goes to leak sites and Telegram/social channels. Leaked material has been reused by other Iran-linked personas, for example Cyber Avengers in October 2023 [S8][S11][S12].

campaigns.name: Moses Staff emerges; encrypt-and-leak against Israeli companies
campaigns.summary: The persona appears and begins attacks on Israeli organizations using PyDCrypt and DCSrv, leaking data without demanding ransom.

campaigns.name: Claimed Israeli Defense Ministry leak
campaigns.summary: Media reported that the group leaked alleged Israeli Defense Ministry files, including photos of the Defense Minister and IDF deployment details. Authenticity is not confirmed in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Check Point exposes MosesStaff ('Ideology over Money')
campaigns.summary: Check Point Research publishes the group's TTPs: Exchange exploitation, web shells, PyDCrypt and DCSrv/DiskCryptor encryption.

campaigns.name: StrifeWater RAT and wider targeting
campaigns.summary: Cybereason reports the StrifeWater RAT and targeting outside Israel in government, finance, travel, energy, manufacturing and utilities.

campaigns.name: Israeli power-plant document leak
campaigns.summary: Moses Staff publishes documents from an Israeli power plant. Cyber Avengers recycled the same material in October 2023.

campaigns.name: Abraham's Ax persona and Saudi ministries
campaigns.summary: A new persona, Abraham's Ax, appears and targets Saudi government ministries. Secureworks links it to Moses Staff/COBALT SAPLING.

campaigns.name: Jerusalem bombing CCTV footage claim
campaigns.summary: Moses Staff posts footage of the 23 November Jerusalem bombing and claims it hacked security cameras. Israeli police and the municipality denied the footage came from their cameras.

campaigns.name: Microsoft names the actor Marigold Sandstorm
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's naming guidance lists Marigold Sandstorm (DEV-0500), which MITRE maps to Moses Staff.

campaigns.name: Moses Staff leaks recycled by Cyber Avengers
campaigns.summary: After 7 October, Cyber Avengers claimed an Israeli power-plant hack using documents Moses Staff had published in June 2022. Kaspersky found no evidence that the two groups are linked. Microsoft calls both IRGC-run personas.

diamond.adversary: Operators of the Moses Staff and Abraham's Ax personas. Microsoft tracks the cluster as Marigold Sandstorm and calls Moses Staff IRGC-run [S4][S8]. Secureworks calls the operator COBALT SAPLING [S10].
diamond.capability: Exchange/public-facing exploitation, obfuscated web shells, PyDCrypt, DCSrv (DiskCryptor-based full-disk encryption), StrifeWater RAT, PsExec, and hack-and-leak publicity [S1][S2][S3][S12].
diamond.infrastructure: Web shells on compromised IIS/Exchange servers and StrifeWater C2 [S1][S2][S3]. Leak sites shared across personas, plus Telegram and X accounts used for claims [S8][S12].
diamond.victim: Mainly Israeli companies and government-linked entities. Also organizations in Italy, India, Germany, Chile, Turkey, the UAE and the US, and Saudi ministries via Abraham's Ax [S1][S3][S10].
diamond.socioPolitical: Anti-Israel hack-and-leak meant to cause damage and psychological effect rather than profit [S1][S2]. Abraham's Ax aims to disrupt Israel-Saudi normalization [S10]. The personas give Iran deniability within IRGC influence activity [S8][S10].
diamond.technology: Unpatched internet-facing Exchange/IIS servers, Windows networks reachable over SMB, RPC and NetBIOS, and abuse of signed DiskCryptor drivers [S1][S2].

gaps: Primary vendor reports could not be opened (host blocked): Check Point (2021-11-15), Cybereason StrifeWater (2022-02-01), Secureworks/Sophos Abraham's Ax analysis (Sophos blog URL could not be confirmed and was removed), Kaspersky Securelist (2023-10), and Fortinet's 'Guard Your Drive from DriveGuard' blog. Their content is cited from MITRE summaries or search-result excerpts only. DriveGuard capabilities and any Moses Staff link from Fortinet are not reflected.

Cluster boundaries: Microsoft's February 2024 report names the persona 'Moses Staff' and not Marigold Sandstorm [S8]. The Marigold Sandstorm-Moses Staff equivalence rests on MITRE and MISP mappings [S1][S7]. Whether Microsoft's Marigold Sandstorm also covers Abraham's Ax is not stated in the sources gathered.

Microsoft says the persona is IRGC-run [S8], whereas the Malek Team persona in the same report is attributed to MOIS. The specific IRGC component and Microsoft's confidence level are not public in the sources gathered.
Kaspersky found no evidence linking Cyber Avengers to Moses Staff even though Microsoft calls both IRGC-run [S8][S11]. Treat them as separate clusters.
MISP Galaxy notes TTP overlaps between Moses Staff and BiBiGun (BiBi wipers, late 2023) [S7]. Not verified in primary reporting; do not merge.
Victim claims (Defense Ministry files, Israel Electric/Dorad, engineering firms, CCTV) are largely self-reported by the persona. Israeli officials disputed the CCTV hack [S12][S13].
No Marigold Sandstorm or Moses Staff activity from 2024 to 2026, including during the June 2025 Israel-Iran conflict, was found in the sources searched.
The aliases COBALT SAPLING and Abraham's Ax come from Secureworks reporting carried in secondary coverage. Neither MITRE nor Microsoft's mapping lists them [S1][S4][S10].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Key terrain is internet-facing Exchange/IIS servers and flat Windows networks where SMB and RPC can be opened between hosts [S1][S2]. Israeli and partner-nation government, energy, utility and manufacturing organizations make up the relevant part of the environment, along with Saudi ministries via the Abraham's Ax persona [S1][S3][S10]. STEP 2 (effects): Whole-disk encryption with no recovery path works as a wiper. Leaks and Telegram claims add an influence layer that IRGC-linked media amplify, so perceived effects can exceed real ones [S1][S2][S8]. STEP 3 (adversary template): exploit an Exchange server, drop an obfuscated web shell, run StrifeWater reconnaissance, steal data, then spread PyDCrypt via opened firewall rules and PsExec. This ends in time-triggered DCSrv encryption and a public leak through persona channels [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is hack-and-leak with destructive encryption against Israeli entities, timed to political events, with claims recycled by sister personas [S8][S11][S12]. MDCOA is the same template against partner-nation energy or utility providers supporting coalition operations, combined with false or exaggerated outage claims to shape perceptions during a crisis [S8]. Candidate indicators: new ASPX files under IIS aspnet_client paths, bulk netsh firewall changes that allow SMB/RPC/NetBIOS, DiskCryptor drivers on servers, StrifeWater beacons, and Moses Staff or Abraham's Ax Telegram/X posts naming a partner organization [S1][S2][S3][S12].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track patch status of internet-facing Exchange/IIS assets across DODIN and mission-partner enclaves, and monitor persona leak channels as early warning [S1][S2][S12]. (2) Authorities: no-ransom encryption is destructive state-linked activity rather than criminal extortion [S1][S8]. Responses may need DCO and interagency coordination, and public attribution claims should credit the assessing source (Microsoft, Secureworks). (3) Mission assurance: keep offline backups and recovery plans for full-disk encryption, and segment networks to resist bulk SMB/RPC firewall changes [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: Israeli and Gulf partners are primary targets [S1][S10]. Share indicators with coalition CERTs, and coordinate public messaging to counter exaggerated persona claims amplified by IRGC-linked media [S8].

provenance.importedSummary: Cybereason Nocturnus describes Moses Staff as an Iranian hacker group, first spotted in October 2021. Their motivation appears to be to harm Israeli companies by leaking sensitive, stolen data.
